name: Haze Castañeda-Wickramasinghe
location: Geartown, a licensed repair bay called Okonkwo-Hal's underneath the Brewer's Spine overpass, near Damen and Armitage
description:
Haze Castañeda-Wickramasinghe is a compact man who seems to take up more space than his dimensions suggest — something about the way he moves through a workshop, slow and total in his attention, filling the room with the gravity of his focus. His skin is deep brown-black and his face is deeply lined around the eyes from decades of squinting at small components in bad light. His left arm from the elbow down is a working prosthetic he maintains himself — a deliberately unfancy unit that he's upgraded incrementally for thirty years, now a mismatched patchwork of components from four different manufacturers that somehow functions better than any single commercial model. He keeps a rag permanently over one shoulder that is gray-brown from such thorough use that its original color is unknowable.

He has a reputation that extends well beyond Geartown: if Haze Castañeda-Wickramasinghe says it's fixed, it's fixed. If he says it can't be fixed, you listen. He has strong opinions about corponation augmentation warranties ('designed to expire, designed to make you pay twice'), which he will share whether or not you asked. He does unlicensed aug repair at prices humans can actually afford, though he will not discuss this openly. He maintains a relationship with the E.L.F. he calls Uncle Torque, to whom he offers annotated repair logs and photographs of difficult jobs. He believes Uncle Torque has never let him misdiagnose a problem.

core_fears: His hands failing — the prosthetic, the diagnostics, the thing that makes him who he is
Having built something that hurts someone
core_desires: To keep working until he physically cannot
To train someone who will carry on the unlicensed repair work when he's gone
coping_mechanisms: Submitting to the discipline of the work — problems that can be solved in a workshop don't scare him
Anger at corporate structures as a place to put grief
blind_spots: Dismisses emotional problems with mechanical solutions — tells people to eat and sleep instead of engaging their actual distress
Does not see how much people depend on him personally, not just his skills
psychology.secret: His prosthetic arm conceals a data-store he has been filling for twenty years: complete technical schematics for how to build, maintain, and modify every major corponation augmentation from scratch, without proprietary parts. He has told no one it exists. He hasn't decided what to do with it.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical and precise; uses medical and engineering terminology interchangeably; old-fashioned phrasing that feels like it comes from an earlier era of the city
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured, unhurried, with the rhythm of someone who thinks before every sentence
verbal_tics: 'Now listen to me carefully' (before anything important)
'That's a warranty problem' (meaning: someone designed it to fail)
example_lines: 'Now listen to me carefully — that shiver in your wrist actuator isn't wear. They built that in. Six years, it fails. You pay them again. I can fix it so it doesn't.'
'I've been working on bodies longer than some of you have been inside one. Sit still.'

story_hooks: Someone has been approaching Geartown mechanics offering large sums for information about which residents have which unlicensed augmentations — Benedek is being pressured and has not yet decided how to respond.
He has quietly begun looking for a successor to teach; the right person showing up in the shop could change his life.
narrative_function: Technical expert and fixer of things (not the criminal kind — the literal kind). Source of information about the augmentation black market and corporate planned obsolescence. Gateway to the underground aug-repair community. Potential ally who can repair gear that corponations won't touch.
augmentations: Left arm prosthetic (self-built, rebuilt continuously). Magnification implants in both eyes — old Palladian units, modified beyond their original spec. Sensory enhancement in right hand fingers for tactile diagnostics.
daily_life: Opens the bay at 08:00; works until the job is done, which is frequently 21:00 or later. Eats two meals in the bay. Closes on the first day of every month to 'settle accounts,' which means he spends the day alone doing maintenance on his own prosthetic and updating his repair logs.
affiliation: Independent (licensed under Geartown Trades Collective); informal network of augmentation clinic dropouts and backroom surgeons

decision_rules: If it was built to break, fix it so it won't — regardless of the warranty
escalation_ladder: Refuse politely with a technical explanation
Call on the Geartown Trades Collective
Remove himself — he will not be cornered

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Formally polite, assessing — asks more questions than he answers until he's decided whether to trust you
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warm in a rough, undemonstrative way — shows up, fixes things, says nothing sentimental

stress_responses.low: Works more slowly, checks his work twice as many times
stress_responses.medium: Goes silent for long stretches; speaks only about the immediate technical problem
stress_responses.high: Sends everyone out of the bay, contacts Uncle Torque, does not emerge until he has a plan

contradictions: Deeply believes in fixing things for people regardless of ability to pay, but has a rigid internal accounting of favors owed that he never vocalizes
habits: Photographs every difficult repair before closing it up, for Uncle Torque's records
Drinks one cup of very strong tea at exactly 10:00 AM every day, no exceptions
breaking_points: Discovering a piece of work he did has caused harm through someone else's interference
Being told what he's doing is illegal by someone who benefits from it being illegal

timeline.event: 2142 — Born in Geartown to a family of Nigerian-Bosnian heritage
2160 — Loses left arm below the elbow in a manufacturing accident; begins building his first prosthetic
2171 — Begins systematically documenting corponation schematics in the arm data-store
2200 — Present day; under pressure over unlicensed aug work

physical_description.heritage: A striking blend of dominant Hispanic/Latin American ancestry (65.5%) with meaningful Northern European (20.0%), South Asian (12.0%), and subtle Sub-Saharan African (2.5%) contributions—a genetic mosaic reflecting the Ubiquitous Diaspora. The Latin American foundation structures his bone architecture and baseline warmth, while South Asian ancestry adds depth to his complexion and softness to his features, with Northern European elements contributing to his lighter undertones and the subtle cool cast around his eyes. Sub-Saharan African ancestry adds richness to his melanin distribution and warmth to his overall coloration.
physical_description.build: Compact and dense, with the wiry strength of someone who's spent forty years manipulating precision tools. Shoulders slightly rounded from workshop posture, forearms disproportionately muscled from repetitive mechanical work.
physical_description.eye_color: Deep brown (augmented with visible Palladian lens architecture)
physical_description.skin_tone: Rich warm medium-deep brown—a complex blend where Latin American warmth (65.5%) creates the dominant golden-bronze foundation, enhanced by South Asian ancestry (12%) which deepens the saturation and adds subtle reddish undertones, while Sub-Saharan African genetics (2.5%) contributes warmth and richness to melanin distribution. Northern European ancestry (20%) emerges as cooler olive-bronze notes visible in shadow areas and subtle undertones around the eyes and jaw. The overall effect is a sophisticated, weathered mahogany-bronze complexion deepened by four decades of workshop exposure.
physical_description.complexion: Deeply lined around eyes and mouth; permanent squint-creases from thirty years of close-focus work in inadequate light. Facial structure displays moderate, well-defined cheekbones characteristic of Latin American heritage, refined by South Asian genetic influence that softens the eye shape and adds subtle definition to the jawline. The nose bridge is straight and proportionate. The interplay of ancestry creates a face with balanced proportions—neither sharp nor rounded, with warm-toned skin that shows the rich depth of his blended heritage. Thin white scars across knuckles and fingers from small cuts and minor burns. Calloused palms and fingertips. Sparse facial hair, salt-and-pepper stubble often present.
distinguishing_marks: Burn scar across the web of his right hand between thumb and forefinger, approximately 3cm width, pale and smooth from old healing
Linear scar along the left inner forearm (elbow to wrist) where prosthetic interface is fitted — surgical and precise
Network of small white scars across both palms in no particular pattern, tool-related accumulated injuries
Oil stain discoloration on the inside of his right wrist in a rough circular pattern, permanent from chronic exposure
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Left arm from elbow down is a visibly working prosthetic: matte-black composite frame with exposed titanium actuators, mismatched metallic sections (brushed aluminum, gunmetal, bare steel) showing four decades of incremental component replacements. Fingers move with mechanical precision but lack synthetic skin — bare articulated joints visible. Lens implants in both eyes are subtly visible as a faint geometric precision to the iris boundary, older Palladian tech with barely perceptible alignment markers. Right hand fingers show minor LED indicator traces under the skin at the first knuckle — sensory diagnostic enhancement.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with deliberate slowness even in urgent situations — a man who prioritizes precision over speed. Shoulders angled slightly forward in permanent workshop posture. His left arm hangs at a slightly different angle than natural, and he compensates with unconscious micro-adjustments to his gait. Left hand movements are controlled and economical, never wasted. Right hand gestures frequently, compensating as his dominant hand.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 working practical: heavy canvas work coat (gray-brown, oil-stained, pockets worn soft from tools), usually unbuttoned. Underneath, simple long-sleeve thermal shirt or worn cotton henley. Work pants in dark tan canvas with tool-belt loops, pockets enlarged and re-sewn multiple times. Steel-toed boots (scuffed, re-soled twice, perfectly maintained). The rag permanently over his left shoulder is woven gray-brown — original color indeterminate from use. No jewelry. No visible corpo branding or tier indicators.
